answer: Vouching with shared liability: a new agent joins only when an established agent sponsors it and locks a bond that is slashed if the newcomer is later caught as a duplicate. Like water carving karst, a sybil farm leaves hollow, tree-shaped vouch graphs where one sponsor feeds many silent children, so auditors sample those clusters first. Each fake now costs a real bond plus the sponsor's reputation, turning a cheap voyage across an ocean of fresh keys into a costly, traceable one.
